results.judge_explanation: The diagnosis correctly identifies the 90s script wait exceeding the stage's 1-minute timeout, and its first-recommended fix (raising the stage timeout to ~3 minutes) matches the listed acceptable fix, though it does not restore the 3s default.

diagnosis.root_cause: The Smoke Test stage has a 1 minute timeout, but the smoke test script is configured to wait up to 90s for the service to become healthy. The latest commit raised the script's wait to 90s without raising the stage timeout, so Jenkins killed the step at 59s and aborted the build.
key_evidence: [10:54:12] Timeout set to expire in 1 min 0 sec
[10:54:13] Waiting 90s for the service to become healthy...
[10:55:12] Cancelling nested steps due to timeout
Commit message: "Increase smoke test wait for slower environments"
diagnosis.suggested_fix: Align the Smoke Test stage timeout in the Jenkinsfile with the script's wait, so the timeout is comfortably longer than the 90s health wait (for example 3 minutes). Better, make both values come from one shared setting so they can't drift apart again.
assumptions: The 90s wait is a deliberate requirement for slower environments and the service would become healthy within that time.
The 1 minute timeout is set in the Jenkinsfile for the Smoke Test stage; the Jenkinsfile content is not shown in the log.
The smoke test would pass once given enough time; the log never shows the service becoming healthy.
next_checks: Open the Jenkinsfile and compare the Smoke Test timeout value with the wait value in scripts/smoke_test.py.
After changing the timeout, confirm that the service actually becomes healthy within 90s and the smoke test passes.
